chunks: Ash-Sharif ar-Radi says: And I say: In this brief speech, there is [beauty] that the places of appreciation cannot reach.
And the portion of amazement aroused by it is greater than the portion of appreciation accorded to it.
And in it, despite the state we have described, there are excesses of eloquence that a tongue cannot express.
Nor can the depth of a human reach it.
And no one will understand what I am saying except one who has practiced this art truly.
And has walked its path with familiarity.
“... No one appreciates it except those who know”
ai.seo_question: What does Ash-Sharif ar-Radi say about the depth of eloquence in the speech?
ai.summary: Ash-Sharif ar-Radi, in his introduction to this sermon, highlights the transcendent eloquence of Imam Ali's speech, suggesting its rhetorical perfection surpasses ordinary human comprehension. He emphasizes that true appreciation requires not just linguistic skill but deep scholarly mastery of the 'science of eloquence' (ilm al-balagha). This meta-commentary serves to elevate the text's status, framing it as a divine gift of wisdom accessible primarily to the learned.

en.sayed-ali-raza: ash-Sharif ar-Raḍī says: In this small speech there is more beauty than can be appreciated,
and the quantity of amazement aroused by it is more than the appreciation accorded to it.
Despite what we have stated it has so many aspects of eloquence that cannot be expressed
nor can anyone reach its depth,
and no one can understand what I am saying
unless one has attained this art and known its details.
“... No one appreciates it except those who know” (Qur’ān, 29:43)
